claim: For complex square quantum channels on \(M_d(\mathbb C)\) of exact Choi/Kraus rank \(r\), any fixed probe set that identifies every rank-\(r\) channel among all CPTP channels must contain at least \[\left\lceil\frac{2d^2r-d^2-r^2}{d^2-1}\right\rceil\] input states. In particular, the universal minimum for exact rank-three qubit channels is four: every fixed triple fails for at least one rank-three channel, while four linearly independent qubit density matrices identify every qubit channel. For any fixed triple, the rank-three qubit channels with locally at least two-dimensional same-output fibers form an open dense subset of each connected component of the exact-rank-three channel manifold.

correctness.rationale: The fixed-rank CPTP manifold has real dimension \(2d^2r-d^2-r^2\). A k-probe output tuple lies in an affine space of dimension at most k(d^2-1). Invariance of domain rules out universal injectivity when the former exceeds the latter. For \(d=2,r=3\) this is \(11>9\); four linearly independent qubit states span Hermitian \(M_2\), proving sufficiency. The analytic maximal-rank locus and constant-rank theorem yield generic fiber dimension at least \(11-9=2\) for any fixed triple.

value.rationale: Minimal probe design is a direct operational question in quantum channel identification and control. The rank-three qubit stratum is the next nontrivial case beyond the recent rank-two result; the theorem gives an exact universal count and quantifies generic three-probe ambiguity as at least two continuous dimensions, which prevents under-designing a fixed-state identification protocol.
